cluePool.definition: The process of writing instructions that tell a computer how to perform a task
Writing software that interacts directly with hardware and manages a computer's operating system.
Designed to be useful for many different types of tasks rather than just one specific job.
Created or planned for a specific purpose or task.
A formal set of rules and symbols used to write instructions that a computer can understand and execute.
The main software that manages a computer's hardware and provides a platform for other programs to run. (e.g., Windows, Unix)
A set of connected things or software that work together as a whole
Created or built over a period of time
The complete process of designing, writing, testing, and maintaining computer programs
The physical, tangible parts of a computer system (like the motherboard or processor)
The electronic component where a computer stores data and instructions temporarily or permanently
The main chip in a computer that executes instructions and processes data (the CPU)
A type of programming language that interacts directly with the computer's hardware, making it difficult for humans to read but highly efficient for machines.
A type of programming language that is easy for humans to read and write, hiding hardware details
Code that is organized in a clear, logical, and modular way
Software designed in separate, independent parts or modules that can be combined
The specific set of rules and structure that dictate how code must be written in a language
The ability of a software program to run on different types of computers or operating systems without major changes
The hardware or software environments on which a program runs
A computer program designed to perform a specific task for the user (like a web browser or word processor)
The programs, data, and instructions that tell a computer what to do
Symbols (like +, -, *, /) that perform mathematical or logical operations on data
Raw facts, numbers, or text that a computer processes
A classification that defines what kind of value a variable can hold, such as numbers or text
A data structure that stores a collection of items of the same type in a single variable
A variable that stores the exact memory address of another variable
A specific format for organizing and storing data in a computer so it can be accessed efficiently
The part of a program that dictates the order in which instructions are executed (like 'if' statements or loops)
The order in which a computer executes the instructions in a program
A small computer system built inside another device (like a smartwatch or car engine) to perform a specific task
How well a program uses computer resources like time and memory without wasting them
The quality of being easy to understand and use
A change or adjustment made to a program's code
An electronic device that accepts data, processes it, and stores the results
A reusable block of code that performs a specific task, often called a function
A single, complete instruction in a program that tells the computer to perform a specific action
